reviews.comment: One of the most poorly designed classes ever. The structure makes it a pain to learn anything at all. Practice was nothing like the final. Professor refused to give us a good idea of what would show up on quizzes and the final. She does a decent job but its pick your poison with the professors for this class. Vague professor with poor course design

Bhargava is one of the best profs for 321. Doesn't mean the class will be easy, and there is tedious work often, but you're in good hands with Bhargava. She provides notes to fill out, she will give out extra credit for attendance sometimes. But mostly, she is an enthusiastic lecturer, and is the prof you should take for 321.

AERO 321 - If she is teaching a class you need, take her. Very good lectures with note packets, not an outrageous amount of homework, clear grading. You learn a lot without suffering! (I also had her for 201 and that was just as good)

Dr. Bhargava has a very clear, concise, organized teaching style which is perfect for a dense subject such as 321. The course is very well organized, and her lecture notes are well designed and super helpful.
Really good lecturer and good lecture slides, she explains everything really well, but I found her classwork relatively harder than the other profs. Def. reccomend her but there are easier profs.

She was a great professor I'd say, but her quizzes and exams were hard. That simple. You've gotta study a lot, read in between the lines for everything honestly cos she picks out the most unexpected stuff for exams and quizzes.

many mandatory outside-of-class assignments (going to meetings / attending presentations, etc.) 20-30% of test/quiz scores are just memorizing plane/rocket names that you have to identify by picture. homework is pretty easy, but does require 2 different textbooks, zero lenience / partial credit. finished with a 79.8 and got a C.

Decent lectures. Reading is no longer required. Exams/quizzes require alot of memorization, and you will be tested on super random things you might overlook, which gets annoying. Class isn't too hard but you need to be giving 100% all the way thru for a good grade. She can be harsh but often its warranted (Ex. ppl talking over her get called out).

Dr. Bhargava is a WONDERFUL professor. The workload is pretty steep but that's just the content of the class. It's not her fault. She cares about her students so so much. I took her a few semesters ago and she still walks by me and recognizes me. She is a wonderful person and a wonderful professor
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took her for AERO321. Dr. Bhargava is an awesome teacher. She really cares about her students. Go to office hours and she will answer your questions and will give homework extensions if you are having trouble. She has fill-in-the-blank notes prepared every class and she is good speaker.

You'd have to attend lectures since notes aren't online. Quizzes harder than exams. With 2 exams, screwing up one *heavily* could be unclutchable (same syllabus for all 201). Get ready to read every 1-2 weeks as 10% of your grade is dependent on it. Since the exams were online, no partial credit. Lots of memorization. There is no extra credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is harder to do well in than it needs to be and she doesn't make it any better. She provides study guides for quizzes and exams so it's easier to study for, but the class relies on a lot of meaningless conventions and things that will make you lose a lot of points. She makes this class a huge pain to be in despite how easy it is.

Lots of reading and long notes packets which can only be filled out in class. Picks favorites and depending on how much she likes you determines the quality and amount of help you get. Unclear grading instructions and long homeworks. Exams are unclear and also very long with a lot of memorization. grades very harsh and doesn't give partial credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
The quizzes feel more challenging than the exam.
Questions are more detailed and sometimes tricky in wording.
A significant amount of reading is required.
Managing the workload and retaining key information can be overwhelming.
